previous_disclosures.summary: The decrease in the effective tax rate in fiscal year 2023 compared to 2022 was primarily due to increased benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and U.S. federal research tax credit, partially offset by higher U.S. taxable earnings and lower one-time benefits from the 2022 subsidiary domestication.

The fiscal year 2023 effective tax rate was lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due to tax benefits from the FDII deduction, stock-based compensation, and the U.S. federal research tax credit.

In 2024, the rate drivers shifted to decreased benefits from FDII/SBC/R&D credits, partially offset by the IRS audit resolution (M0357). The change in the composition of tax rate drivers, particularly the move from one-time domestication benefits to structural credit reductions and audit settlements, meaningfully changes the understanding of the company's tax position and future trends.

comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rate
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 with a 19% effective tax rate, compared to a $346 million benefit and (68%) rate in 2023. The 2024 provision increase was driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose specific drivers for their 2024 effective tax rates under Item 7. NVDA attributes its rate to a $145 million benefit from an IRS audit resolution which partially offset decreases in benefits from FDII, stock-based compensation, and research credits. In contrast, AMD's 2024 provision of $381 million (19% effective rate) was driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction. While both companies report 2024 effective tax rates influenced by specific discrete or structural items (audit resolution for NVDA, integration transaction for AMD), the nature and magnitude of these impacts differ significantly: NVDA's audit resolution provided a net benefit helping to keep its rate below the statutory rate, whereas AMD's integration transaction increased its provision significantly compared to the prior year's benefit.

sentences.text: The increase in the effective tax rate was partially offset by a benefit due to the IRS audit resolution.
Our effective tax rate for fiscal year 2024 was additionally benefited by the IRS audit resolution.
We recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2023, representing effective tax rates of 19% and (68%), respectively.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
